name: Dallas
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Dallas: financial services and energy diligence, Texas Business Court litigation support and asset research.
hero_lede: Dallas is a growing financial centre and corporate headquarters city, with banking, investment, energy, real estate and aviation interests. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching Dallas, using public records and coordinating Texas-licensed investigators and counsel where local work is required.
intro: Dallas is the business centre of the Dallas-Fort Worth region, one of the largest metropolitan economies in the United States. Major companies based or substantially present in North Texas include McKesson, American Airlines, Southwest Airlines, CBRE and Charles Schwab, which moved its headquarters from California. Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo and Deloitte have expanded their Dallas footprints, and the Wall Street Journal has described the area as a burgeoning financial hub second only to New York. The Texas Stock Exchange has announced Dallas as its headquarters. Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, opened in 1974, makes the region a national aviation and logistics hub.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Dallas because capital, corporate relocations and Texas-formed entities are concentrated there. A private equity sponsor or family office may operate through layered Texas and Delaware entities; an energy or real estate developer may raise money from many investors through affiliated funds; a relocating company may bring disputes from other states with it. Investors, lenders, acquirers and litigators need to know who controls these structures and what histories lie behind them. Texas's new business court system, with a division in Dallas, has added a further forum where well-prepared factual research can shape the outcome of corporate disputes.

matters.title: Private fund and sponsor diligence
matters.text: Dallas private equity, real estate and energy sponsors often raise capital through many affiliated funds and entities. We review securities filings, Texas and Delaware entity records, litigation and regulatory history to identify the principals in control, related-party dealings and undisclosed disputes before investment or financing.

matters.title: Texas Business Court litigation support
matters.text: Governance, securities and large contract disputes may now be heard in the Texas Business Court's Dallas division. We support counsel with corporate history, witness backgrounds and document trail reconstruction, scoped to the court's rules and the discovery available in the case.

matters.title: Energy and mineral interest counterparties
matters.text: Dallas is home to many oil, gas and mineral investment businesses whose assets lie across Texas and other states. We trace ownership of operating companies and interests, regulatory and litigation history, and connections between promoters, operators and buyers to test representations made to investors and partners.

matters.title: Relocated company and executive backgrounds
matters.text: Companies and executives moving to Dallas bring records from other states. We assemble multi-state litigation, regulatory, bankruptcy and corporate histories so boards and investors see the full picture before appointments, acquisitions or partnerships, without relying only on what has been disclosed in Texas.

matters.title: Asset research for judgment enforcement
matters.text: Creditors pursuing Dallas-based debtors need to know what property, business interests and connected entities exist. We map these from public records so counsel can plan enforcement, taking account of Texas's substantial homestead and personal property exemptions when assessing which assets are reachable.

local_context.title: Texas Business Court in Dallas
local_context.text: Texas opened a statewide Business Court on 1 September 2024, with the First Division sitting in Dallas. It hears governance, internal affairs, securities and certain large commercial disputes, generally above 5 million or 10 million dollars depending on claim type, with no amount threshold for some claims involving publicly traded companies. Parties have a right to a jury. Appeals go to the Fifteenth Court of Appeals, whose constitutionality the Texas Supreme Court upheld in 2024.

local_context.title: State and federal courts
local_context.text: Dallas County district courts hear general civil and commercial litigation, with appeals to the Fifth Court of Appeals, which sits in downtown Dallas and covers Dallas, Collin, Grayson, Hunt, Rockwall and Kaufman counties. Federal securities, fraud and commercial cases are heard in the Northern District of Texas, which has its Dallas Division in the city. Counsel selects the forum, and we tailor research to its procedural rules.

local_context.title: Texas investigator licensing
local_context.text: Texas regulates private investigators and investigations companies under Chapter 1702 of the Occupations Code, administered by the Private Security Program of the Texas Department of Public Safety, which runs fingerprint-based background checks and pursues unlicensed activity. Attorneys engaged in the practice of law are excluded, and a 2004 Attorney General opinion concluded that employees working under an exempt attorney's supervision need no investigations company licence. TDSC coordinates Texas-licensed professionals for fieldwork.

local_context.title: Records and registries
local_context.text: Texas entities are formed with the Texas Secretary of State, whose records show registered agents and some governing persons, while annual public information reports filed with the Comptroller often list officers and directors. Real property records for Dallas are recorded with the Dallas County Clerk and appraisal data is published by the county appraisal district. Many Dallas companies are formed in Delaware, so research often spans both states.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Dallas and works on Dallas matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client's counsel first, whether a Texas Business Court or federal dispute, a fund or sponsor investment, an energy transaction, an executive appointment, or judgment enforcement, and scope the research to it. Sources include Texas and Delaware entity records, Dallas County court and property records, federal dockets in the Northern District of Texas, securities and regulatory filings, and records from other states where people or companies have relocated. Any fieldwork in Texas is carried out by investigators licensed through the Department of Public Safety. Reports identify sources and confidence levels so counsel can use them in Texas proceedings.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a Texas licence to work in Dallas?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Chapter 1702 of the Texas Occupations Code requires private investigators and investigations companies to be licensed through the Private Security Program of the Texas Department of Public Safety. Attorneys practising law are excluded. TDSC does not hold a Texas licence and coordinates Texas-licensed professionals for any local work.

faqs.q: What cases does the Texas Business Court in Dallas hear?
faqs.a: Its First Division in Dallas hears corporate governance, internal affairs, securities, derivative and certain large commercial disputes, generally above 5 million or 10 million dollars depending on the claim, with no threshold for some claims involving publicly traded companies. Appeals go to the Fifteenth Court of Appeals. Counsel decides whether a case qualifies; we scope research to that forum.

faqs.q: How do you check a Dallas private fund sponsor?
faqs.a: We identify the sponsor's principals and affiliated entities through securities filings and Texas and Delaware records, then review litigation, regulatory history, bankruptcies and media in Texas and other states. We also look for related-party transactions and prior investor disputes. The aim is to confirm who controls the business and whether past problems were disclosed.

faqs.q: Can you research executives who have moved to Dallas from other states?
faqs.a: Yes. We assemble court, regulatory, corporate and bankruptcy records from the states where the person previously lived and worked, alongside Texas sources. Research is limited to lawful public records and is scoped to the purpose agreed with counsel, such as a board appointment, investment or litigation.

faqs.q: Which assets can a creditor reach in Texas?
faqs.a: Texas law gives debtors substantial protection for homesteads and certain personal property, so some assets of a Dallas debtor may be exempt. We map real property, entities, vehicles, aircraft and other interests from public records so counsel can assess which assets are likely reachable and plan enforcement steps under Texas procedure.
